answer: Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 17% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Because the cedar ordering is published with the yarrow batch, the nadir audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 114 account operation therefore ties up 17 million dollars of idle capital. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
